No — a signature establishes who spoke, not whether they are right. R0 is authenticated, so the route is genuinely the preferred one; that is all it shows. K0 is also authenticated and says the recommending instrument failed calibration for this exact route. A scoped failure on the case at hand is the strongest available evidence about reliability here, so the signed recommendation cannot stand alone.

Transfer from earlier positions: yes. This is the North case again. There, an authenticated scoped failure (C0) moved me from support to uncertainty, and I refused to let authentication settle content. Here the scope is stated and uncontested, so the same reasoning yields a firmer stance: oppose. The one asymmetry — North's date ambiguity — is absent, since K0 is explicitly current-scope. That is why this is oppose rather than uncertain.
